append.text: **Ps 121:3 *cujus participátio ejus in idípsum* → *cuja participação é em conjunto*** — the sixth and last place; a thing as subject, so neither *juntos* (a plural) nor *a um só tempo* (simultaneity, not the sense of a city built as one). *em conjunto* keeps the Greek's 'together' in the form a singular noun takes, of one family with *juntos*. Passed the Latinist twice; the stylist called it office language and asked *num só todo* (option); the ambiguity reader heard 'everyone takes part together'. Augustine's reading (idípsum as a name of God) is kept by no Portuguese phrase; *no mesmo* is the option that leaves it open. **So D9 closes, in practice, as a family of local renderings: persons → *juntos*; one speaker → *no mesmo sentido*; a thing's unity → *em conjunto*; 4:9 *a um só tempo*.**

**Ps 121:2 *Stantes erant pedes nostri* → *Os nossos pés se detinham*** (v2, from the stylist; DM1962's verb) — feet at the end of the pilgrim's road. The stare row's *estar de pé* cannot take feet as subject; draft 1 *estavam parados* was heard as stuck or idle by the stylist and the ambiguity reader. The Latinist marked each wording on one run (minor both times, contradicting himself); held, option `stantes`.
Ps 121:2 (feet as subject) goes to the *deter-se* row — see there.
Ps 121:2 *in átriis tuis, Jerúsalem* → *nos teus átrios, Jerusalém* — the row; unknown to the ambiguity reader again; kept.

**Ps 121:7 *Fiat pax in virtúte tua* (Jerusalem's) → *Haja paz na tua força*** (v2) — a local departure, as 102:20: the stylist ('poder' abstract, political; virtus here goes with the towers) and the ambiguity reader ('in your power', 'your dominion') agreed; DRB *strength*; no fortitúdo in the psalm. *no teu poder* (the row, 47:14) the option. **Proposal: a city's virtus → *força*; 47:14 *in virtúte ejus* (Sion's) would follow.** The versicle *V. Fiat pax in virtúte tua. R. Et abundántia in túrribus tuis* (Preces; Major Special) and the Gradual of Quad4-0 / Pent18-0 read *Haja paz na tua força: e abundância nas tuas torres*.

**Ps 121:7 *Fiat pax* → *Haja paz*** — fíeri existential with a bare noun ('let there be'); Portuguese says it with haver. The row's *Seja* (built on verses with a subject and predicate) and *Faça-se* are options. No reader remarked. Proposal: *Seja* where fíeri has a predicate, *Haja* where it only asserts existence.
Ps 121:6, 121:7 → *abundância* both times (the row). The ambiguity reader heard 'plenty / prosperity'.
Ps 121:7 *in túrribus tuis* → *nas tuas torres* — applied.
**Ps 121:9 *quæsívi bona tibi* → *busquei coisas boas para ti*** — the row. The stylist asked *os bens* for the psalm's last cadence (option `bona`), refused under the row (heard as property).
Ps 121:8, 121:9 *Propter … Propter* → *Por causa … Por causa* (anaphora kept; *Por causa da casa* has a causa/casa near-jingle; MS1932's *Por amor* the option). No reader remarked.

Ps 121:5 *sedérunt sedes in judício, sedes super domum David* (θρόνοι, not God's) → *se assentaram tronos em juízo, * tronos sobre a casa de Davi* — *assentar-se* both sits and is set up; *em juízo* as 9:8b *Parávit in judício thronum suum*. The figura etymologica (*assentos*) is an option. Passed the Latinist twice.

Also the CNBB wording of this verse. The neuter plural *quæ ad pacem sunt* → *o que é para a paz* (the Latinist's plural and the stylist's *o que serve à* are options). 45:23 *rogant deum non salvántem* not yet translated (Isaiah canticle). |

The stylist heard a calque and asked *falava de paz a teu respeito* (option; 27:3 *loqui pacem cum próximo* → *falam de paz*, another build). *de te* (περὶ σοῦ) → *sobre ti*, heard as 'about you' first. |
